title: Red Watermelon Salad With Raspberry Dressing
notes: Gluten-free, diabetic friendly, raw. Coconut Nectar. Coconut nectar comes from the coconut’s flowers and is used as a natural sweetener. When dehydrated and granulated it becomes coconut sugar. It is low in fructose, unlike agave, and has a low GI (glycemic index) meaning it doesn’t spike blood sugar levels to the extent that some sweeteners do. This said, it is still a sweetener with lots of calories and little additional nutritional value. It has a light maple syrup, earthy flavour with a bittersweet aftertaste. In this recipe, coconut nectar could be substituted for maple syrup, honey or agave syrup.

ingredientSections.heading: Raspberry Dressing
items: 2 Tbsp organic balsamic reduction (blueberry or raspberry)
2 Tbsp cold pressed virgin olive oil

ingredientSections.heading: Watermelon Salad
items: 140g green spring mix salad and watercress

methodSections.heading: Watermelon Salad
steps: Arrange green spring mix salad and watercress on a large serving platter.
Cut the watermelon into 1cm (½in) thick triangles.
Arrange the watermelon triangles on top of the green salad and drizzle with the raspberry dressing.
Halve the raspberries and cherries, removing the pits, and arrange on top of salad. Add the finely chopped basil leaves.
Sprinkle the pomegranate seeds, orange rind and peppercorns over everything and serve.
